components.name: Channel Key (Send)
components.description: Home's SEND key: pixel triangle, channel label, one-line hint.

components.name: Channel Key (Receive)
components.description: Home's RECEIVE key in Phosphor Green.
components.css: .ds-chkey-r { display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:20px; width:328px; height:300px; background:rgba(0,255,0,0.05); color:#00FF00; border:1px solid rgba(0,255,0,0.75); border-radius:0; font-family:'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-tri-down { width:0; height:0; border-left:38px solid transparent; border-right:38px solid transparent; border-top:42px solid #00FF00; } .ds-chkey-r-label { font-size:40px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:6px; } .ds-chkey-r-hint { font-size:18px; } .ds-chkey-r:hover, .ds-chkey-r:focus-visible { outline:1px solid rgba(0,255,0,0.4); outline-offset:-7px; } .ds-chkey-r:active { background:rgba(0,255,0,0.2); border:3px solid #00FF00; }

components.name: Action Button

components.html: <button class="ds-action">CREATE LIGHTNING INVOICE</button> <button class="ds-action" disabled>CREATE LIGHTNING INVOICE</button>
components.css: .ds-action { width:672px; height:112px; margin-bottom:12px; background:rgba(255,170,0,0.05); color:#FFAA00; border:1px solid rgba(255,170,0,0.75); border-left:6px solid rgba(255,170,0,0.45); border-radius:0; font:700 28px 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; letter-spacing:2px; cursor:pointer; } .ds-action:hover, .ds-action:focus-visible { outline:1px solid rgba(255,170,0,0.35); outline-offset:-6px; } .ds-action:active { background:rgba(255,170,0,0.2); border:2px solid #FFAA00; border-left:6px solid #FFAA00; } .ds-action:disabled { background:#000; color:#838383; border-color:rgba(85,85,85,0.6); cursor:not-allowed; }

components.name: Amount Key
components.description: Keypad amount; selected is the reference lit state, disabled marks amounts above the balance.
components.css: .ds-keys { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 216px); gap:12px; } .ds-key { height:114px; background:#000; color:rgba(255,170,0,0.9); border:1px solid rgba(255,170,0,0.6); border-radius:0; font:700 44px 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-key:hover, .ds-key:focus-visible { border-color:#FFAA00; } .ds-key:active { background:rgba(255,170,0,0.25); } .ds-key-on { background:rgba(255,170,0,0.14); color:#FFAA00; border:2px solid #FFAA00; outline:1px solid rgba(255,170,0,0.35); outline-offset:-7px; } .ds-key:disabled { color:#838383; border-color:rgba(85,85,85,0.6); cursor:not-allowed; }

narrative.overview:
The wallet is a monitor in NERV's command centre: a black glass field on which the system reports state. Nothing here decorates for its own sake. Frames, bracket corners, and scanlines exist to make the screen read as an instrument, and every number on it (balance, amount, invoice) reads as a live readout. The mood is urgent, precise, and cinematic: a live operation, where every value matters and every action is announced.

The system runs quiet structure with loud channels. Structure sits back in low-strength hairlines, while channels (send, receive, Lightning, Bluetooth) carry saturated alarm colour. Controls feel like an alarm panel: loud, colour-coded, unmistakable, and big enough for a stranger's thumb. At rest the screen is flat. Under a finger, or when selected, a control lights up like an indicator on a console.

The system is designed natively for one physical object: the 72 × 72 mm HyperPixel 4.0 Square at about 254 PPI. Every size is chosen in millimetres (10px ≈ 1mm), never in desktop pixels. It has one column, no scrolling, and touch only. It must never read as a generic crypto dashboard (gradients, glassy cards, purple-blue fintech sheen, coin logos) or be assembled from stock OS widgets (Material, Fluent, or Cupertino controls).
keyCharacteristics: The whole square is used. Each screen is one full-height stack: header, readout, controls, action, status.
One saturated channel colour per function; orange is the system's own voice.
Uppercase terminal type, bold almost everywhere, with `//` as the separator.
Square corners, 1px hairlines, bracketed corners, stepped pixel icons, scanlines.
Flat at rest, lit on touch: glow is built from frames and tints, never from shadows.

rules.name: The Channel Rule
rules.body: Every function owns exactly one colour, and nothing else wears it: SEND is red, RECEIVE and value are green, Lightning is amber, Bluetooth is blue, and the system is orange. A screen takes its channel's colour in its header bar, its keypad, and its primary action.

rules.name: The Green Means Sats Rule
rules.body: Phosphor Green is reserved for sat amounts, receiving, and success. An amount is green even on the red Send screen.

rules.name: The Strength Ladder Rule
rules.body:
Colours sit on black at stepped strengths, never as blended mid-tones:
- text at 85–100%
- control frames at 60–75% (100% when lit)
- structural hairlines at 12–45%
- tints at 5% at rest, 12–25% when lit or pressed, and 6% for scanlines

rules.name: The Millimetre Rule
rules.body: Size everything physically: 10px ≈ 1mm on this panel. A desktop-sized pixel value is roughly 60% too small here.

rules.name: The 18px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is smaller than 18px (about 1.8mm). Primary labels are 24px or larger.

rules.name: The Terminal Voice Rule
rules.body: Interface text is uppercase, and `//` separates a subject from its qualifier ("SEND // TOKEN", "INVOICE // LIGHTNING"). Hostnames and URLs keep their real case ("mint.minibits.cash").

rules.name: The Built Glow Rule
rules.body: Never use `drop-shadow-*`; it renders nothing here. Light is made of frames and tints.

rules.name: The Lit-On-Active Rule
rules.body: Glow means "active, selected, or under a finger now". A resting element never glows, and a glowing element is always something the user can act on or is currently acting on.

dos: Do size in millimetres: touch targets 80px (8mm) or larger, primary actions 100px or larger, text 18px or larger.
Do fill the square. Let keypads and keys stretch to absorb leftover height instead of leaving empty space below the content.
Do give each screen exactly one channel colour, shown in its header bar, keypad, and primary action.
Do keep Phosphor Green for sats, receiving, and success only.
Do give every control a pressed state and, where it can be unavailable, a disabled state that still explains itself when tapped.
Do build lit states from stacked 1px frames and a stepped tint (see Elevation & Depth).
Do position decorative squares explicitly, or wrap them in a centred `VerticalLayout`. Inside a `HorizontalLayout`, a fixed-size rectangle sits at the top, not the middle.
Do write interface text in uppercase with `//` separators, leaving hostnames in their real case.
donts: Don't carry over desktop pixel sizes. 12px text and 44px targets are about 1.2mm and 4.4mm on this panel.
Don't use `drop-shadow-*`; the software renderer draws nothing.
Don't round a corner, introduce a circle, or use a text glyph (◄, ▶, ✓) as an icon. Draw stepped pixel icons from rectangles.
Don't import `std-widgets.slint` or any Material, Fluent, or Cupertino control.
Don't use gradients, glass or blur, purple-blue fintech colour, or coin logos.
Don't let Pattern Blue stand for anything but Bluetooth, or any channel colour stand for a different function.
Don't set text in Standby Gray (#555555); use Standby Text (#838383).
Don't name a Slint component property `color` on anything that inherits `Rectangle`; it collides with a deprecated built-in and fails the build. Use `tint`.
